title: Minimum Rectangles to Cover Points
summary: Given a 2D integer array of points where each point is represented as [xi, yi], and an integer w, your task is to find the minimum number of rectangles needed to cover all the points.
statement: Given a 2D integer array of points where each point is represented as [xi, yi], and an integer w, your task is to find the minimum number of rectangles needed to cover all the points. Each rectangle must have its lower end at some point (x1, 0) and its upper end at some point (x2, y2), with the conditions that x1 = 0, and x2 - x1 <= w must be satisfied. A point is considered covered if it lies within or on the boundary of a rectangle. Note that a point can be covered by more than one rectangle.
constraints: points is nonempty and w is nonnegative.
A rectangle may have any height and horizontal interval [x1,x2] with x2-x1≤w; its bottom lies on y=0.
Return the minimum number of such rectangles covering every point; only x-coordinates affect coverage.
hints: A rectangle starting at the leftmost uncovered x should extend its full width rightward; moving it left cannot cover any additional remaining point.
Sort x-coordinates and greedily start a rectangle at each first coordinate beyond the current covered boundary.
Maintain coveredRight; when x>coveredRight, increment and set coveredRight=x+w.
The first uncovered point forces a new rectangle, and the greedy placement maximizes its reach without sacrificing any earlier coverage.
editorial: The first uncovered point forces a new rectangle, and the greedy placement maximizes its reach without sacrificing any earlier coverage.

tests.explanation: One rectangle covers x from one through two and another covers three through four, so two suffice.
Intervals [0,2] and [4,6] cover all points with two rectangles.
